rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a participant may perform an action at any time while an ongoing activity of that same participant is running (for example, updating a list during an activity that is still in progress): Model the action as a flow node inside the same process as the participant's lane that holds the ongoing activity. Have that lane reference the node, and connect the node to the ongoing activity's scope so it can occur during that activity. Do not place the action's start or any of its nodes in a separate process or pool, and do not have a lane reference a node that is not defined in its own process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a participant may perform an action at any time while an ongoing activity of that same participant is running (for example, updating a list during an activity that is still in progress)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process begins when a participant performs an action (an activity it names), rather than when an external message, signal, time or condition occurs: Model a start event for the process beginning, with no incoming flow, followed by a task labeled with that participant's action in the description's own wording. Do not label the start event with the action, and do not replace the action with the start event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description's first stated step is a participant's own action (such as finding out or choosing what they want) that has no external message, signal, time or condition as its trigger, and the description does not name a separate external trigger for that action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a person must first find out or decide which items to work on before any automated activity starts: Model that preparatory decision as a userTask performed by the person, placed at the start of the process before the automated activities that depend on its result. Keep it as a distinct element so that the later automated steps follow it, and do not fold it into the first automated activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a person must first find out or decide which items to work on before any automated activity starts

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names one actor who selects or supplies choices and a separate automated actor that carries out the work after those choices are complete, and both act within the same process: Wrap the whole process in one bpmn:participant pool, and model each named actor as its own lane inside that pool. Place the activities the human actor performs (choosing, prioritizing, supplying inputs) and the process start in the human actor's lane. Place the automated work that runs after all choices are collected in the automated actor's lane. Do not leave the automated actor's activities in the human actor's lane, and do not omit the pool or lanes.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names one actor who selects or supplies choices and a separate automated actor that carries out the work after those choices are complete, and both act within the same process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a set of items (up to a stated number) is handled in parallel, with each item in its own branch that must finish before the process continues: Model a parallel gateway that forks into one branch per item being processed in parallel, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches before the shared continuation. Do not use an exclusive gateway for the fork or the join, and do not put decision conditions on the parallel branches. A stated limit on how many items run at once can be shown in the task or the description, not as a gateway condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a set of items (up to a stated number) is handled in parallel, with each item in its own branch that must finish before the process continues

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an ongoing activity is set back by an occasional event, and that the process then goes on with the work that was interrupted: Model the setback as an intermediate event or a recovery task placed where the interruption occurs, and connect the recovery with sequence flow to a task that resumes the interrupted work, so that the remaining work after the interruption is still modeled. Do not let the recovery path end the process unless the description states that outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an ongoing activity is set back by an occasional event, and that the process then goes on with the work that was interrupted

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that after a participant has supplied all of their choices, a separate automated actor acting for that participant starts its work, and the description names no further participant action between the last choice and that start: Connect the last choice task in the participant's lane directly to the start of the automated actor's work in that actor's own lane. Do not add a confirmation or review task in the participant's lane that the description does not state, and do not place the automated actor's start, ongoing work, or checks in the participant's lane.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that after a participant has supplied all of their choices, a separate automated actor acting for that participant starts its work, and the description names no further participant action between the last choice and that start

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an occurrence (such as a checkpoint being reached) can happen at any point while an ongoing activity is running and that the participant is informed of it, and the description does not state that the occurrence starts the process: Model the occurrence as an intermediate catch event placed in the flow of the running activity, not as a start event and not as a separate subprocess. Route the flow so that the running activity continues after the participant has been informed. If the description states that the occurrence is checked before the participant is informed, place an exclusive gateway before the notification step to decide whether the occurrence has happened. Model the notification step as a task labeled with the description's wording for the notification, or as a send task only when the description states a message being sent.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an occurrence (such as a checkpoint being reached) can happen at any point while an ongoing activity is running and that the participant is informed of it, and the description does not state that the occurrence starts the process
